direction_summaries.explanation: It appears that the feature is detecting when a period belongs to a token‐sequence that is an abbreviation or otherwise signals a special “entity boundary” (for example, in “U.S.”, “St. Louis”, or “Oct.”). In these cases the period isn’t acting as a sentence‐end but as part of a formatted or proper name token, so the model’s predictions shift from a more generic continuation (like “vet”) to one that fits a proper noun or numeric entity (such as “S”, “Louis”, “13”, etc.).

When given 'un-known', the model picks up on the morpheme cue '-known' to produce the specific word 'unknown'.
